item.title: Night classes bring culture alive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
If he hadn't tried it himself, Shareef Shabaz, a 24-year-old Pakistani student, would never have guessed that sugar could be more than a sweet treat — it can also become art. The discovery did not come at a tourist stall or a museum, but during a night class in Beijing's Haidian district, where Shabaz drew his first sugar dragon and tried his hand at sugar blowing, a traditional technique used in Chinese sugar art. "If it weren't for this vivid, fun class, I wouldn't have realized Chinese culture is tied to real life so much more than textbooks," Shabaz said. Across China, night classes are giving learners a lighter introduction to Chinese culture. At Shabaz's school, for example, each class attracts 20 to 30 learners from countries such as Pakistan, Russia, Cuba and Sri Lanka. For foreign visitors who want to try such classes, local district authorities' official social media accounts are a good place to look, with QR codes often provided for registration. In Haidian, classes range from tea culture and sugar art to making traditional Chinese clothing. Most of the classes are free. The idea is not necessarily to turn newcomers into experts. A few hours of making something with their own hands can instead give them a reason to start asking questions about the culture behind it. Russian learner Tatiana Kazakevich found that out with a ceramic cup. Before the class, she had seen similar cups with floral motifs in museums but never thought about the meanings behind the patterns. In the class, she followed her teacher, painting lotuses and grapevines on her cup. As the patterns took shape, she started exploring the symbolism behind different floral motifs: the lotus stands for purity, while grapevines represent bonds and togetherness. She also painted a peony after learning that it symbolizes prosperity in China. "Now I see the flowers not just as pretty, but as showing vitality and flourishing life energy," Kazakevich said. "As I made it with my own hands, I felt I was an ancient artisan, as if I was part of Chinese culture." For some learners, a night class can also reveal unexpected connections with their homeland. Madhushani Gunawardhana from Sri Lanka once thought that the culture of her country was vastly different from that of China. But a handicraft night class changed her mind. At the class on chanhua, a traditional Chinese craft of making delicate flowers with wrapped silk, Gunawardhana watched her teacher twist thin threads to form delicate yellow petals. She then picked up the threads herself, and something about the technique felt strangely familiar. "It instantly reminded me of our Beeralu lace in Galle," she said. "It struck me how much traditional heritage can have in common across different cultures and times." That discovery stirred her interest in exploring more of Chinese culture. She said that, given the opportunity, she would like to travel around China and participate in night classes in other cities, hoping to find more moments of cross-cultural dialogue. There are certainly many places to find such moments, as night classes have become a nationwide trend, with programs in cities including Beijing, Shanghai and Chengdu, Sichuan province. This year, Shanghai alone has 1,962 night-class venues, attracting 194,000 learners, according to the Shanghai Observer. Behind the expansion is a broader push to make lifelong learning more accessible. In 2025, China unveiled a national blueprint on building the country into an education powerhouse by 2035. It aims to upgrade public services for lifelong learning and build a learning-oriented society where "everyone can learn, anywhere, anytime". As night classes expand their courses and venues, international learners are also becoming part of that vision of learning beyond conventional classrooms. Meanwhile, as China's visitor-friendly entry policies draw more overseas visitors to the country, trends such as "China Study" and "China Travel" are bringing a growing number of international learners to night classes, and their interests may offer new inspiration for future course design. "I hope night classes can roll out more courses related to AI and the smart economy in the future," said Shabaz from Pakistan. Service info Foreign visitors can sign up for night classes in Beijing's Haidian district via QR codes posted on its official WeChat account, where class schedules are also available. Most classes are free. Other districts in Beijing, including Chaoyang and Xicheng, have released their December night-class schedules. Foreign visitors can find registration information on Beijing Bendibao, a local lifestyle information platform. In Shanghai, night-class listings are available through the official WeChat account of the Shanghai Public Art Center. Shanghai's community night classes cost 500 yuan ($75) for 12 sessions, and are open to all.

item.title: CAR-T expertise draws foreign cancer patients
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
A Romanian patient with a serious form of lymphoma, a type of blood cancer that had returned despite previous treatment, has been discharged from Shanghai Tongji Hospital after receiving an advanced cancer treatment administered by a Chinese medical team. The 58-year-old woman, Sandica-Iuliana Klein, came to Shanghai specifically for treatment this summer. Doctors said she was the hospital's first Romanian patient and may also be the first Romanian to travel to China for CAR-T therapy, an advanced treatment that uses a patient's own immune cells to fight cancer. CAR-T therapy involves collecting immune cells called T cells from a patient's blood, modifying them in a laboratory to help them recognize and attack cancer cells, and then returning them to the patient's body. The treatment essentially equips the body's natural defense system with a more targeted ability to fight tumors. Klein underwent a combination of radiotherapy and CAR-T therapy at the Shanghai hospital. By the time she was discharged, her levels of lactate dehydrogenase, an enzyme in the blood that can indicate the extent of tumor activity, had fallen significantly, suggesting a positive response to treatment. Klein had previously received treatment for lymphoma in Romania and achieved remission, meaning the signs of cancer had disappeared. However, the disease progressed again last year. Further chemotherapy in Romania brought only partial remission, with some cancer remaining. With CAR-T treatment unavailable in her home country, long waiting times in many other countries and relatively few hospitals in Europe offering comprehensive treatment, Klein and her family began looking overseas. They eventually focused on China after learning about Tongji Hospital's experience in CAR-T therapy and its successful treatment of international patients. Through an online medical consultation, they contacted the team led by Li Ping, a professor in the hospital's hematology department. Klein arrived in Shanghai on Aug 22, and her T cells were collected six days later. Li said that she also had scleroderma, a rare condition that causes the skin to become hard and tight, as well as hypothyroidism, in which the thyroid gland does not produce enough hormones to regulate functions such as metabolism. "Using CAR-T treatment for her was like killing multiple birds with one stone, and it really saved her life," Li said. The medical team conducted additional genetic tests and found a mutation that placed Klein at a higher risk of the cancer returning. To reduce that risk, doctors arranged radiotherapy before reinfusing her modified T cells. The aim was to shrink the tumor first, making the subsequent CAR-T treatment more effective and reducing the likelihood of relapse, Li said. "Often the challenge with CAR-T lies not in the reinfusion itself but in the comprehensive management before and after the infusion," she said, emphasizing the importance of careful preparation and follow-up. Klein, whose husband is from the United States, said patients in her home country usually consider seeking advanced treatment in North America. However, she decided on China after comparing treatment costs and medical experience. CAR-T treatment in China costs about one-third of the price in the US, while Chinese hospitals also have extensive experience in administering the therapy, she said. Tongji Hospital was among the first hospitals in China to conduct clinical research on CAR-T therapy, beginning in 2015. The hospital has since treated more than 1,000 patients. More than 100 patients from foreign countries and regions, including Thailand and Singapore, have traveled to the Shanghai hospital specifically for the treatment. "What surprised me the most was how international this hospital is. From the first video call with Professor Li, I felt I could entrust myself to this team. They are professional and gentle, explaining every step clearly, even those test results I failed to understand," Klein said. Following her discharge, Li's team will conduct monthly remote follow-ups for six months and coordinate with hospitals in Romania to arrange further care.

item.title: Nation's opening-up fuels growth across Asia-Pacific
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
China's deepening opening-up and strengthening focus on innovation, advanced manufacturing and green technology are creating new development opportunities across the Asia-Pacific region, business leaders said. Those opportunities are increasingly flowing in both directions as regional markets become more integrated, said Rose Zhu, chief country officer of Deutsche Bank China. "For multinational companies, China remains an important market, innovation hub and part of global supply chains," Zhu said. "We see particularly strong potential along key growth corridors connecting China with other (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation) economies, Europe and the Middle East." At the same time, Chinese companies are increasingly looking overseas to diversify their markets, expand their global footprint and participate more deeply in international value chains, she said. Alan Li, president of CBRE China, said, "Multinationals are no longer chasing low costs." Instead, they are seeking to tap China's advanced technology, talent pool and consumer market, while benefiting from a more open and unified business environment, he said. New office leasing by foreign companies in major Chinese cities rose 26 percent year-on-year in the first half of 2026, the strongest increase since 2022, according to CBRE, a commercial real estate services and investment company headquartered in the United States. Demand was led by financial and professional services, up 31 percent, and consumer-sector companies, up 34 percent. China's supply-chain strengths and talent base have continued to attract investment in advanced manufacturing, particularly in life sciences, advanced equipment and new energy vehicle components, Li said. For multinational manufacturers, China's advantage increasingly lies in the speed at which technology can transition from development to commercial application. "China's strong industrial ecosystem and diverse application scenarios help accelerate testing and adoption at scale," said Hendrik Kohleick, president of Henkel Asia-Pacific. Fast-growing sectors including electric mobility, artificial intelligence, humanoid robotics and data centers are creating demand for new materials and industrial processes that improve performance, efficiency and sustainability, while consumers are seeking more personalized, high-quality and sustainable products, he said. Henkel, a German multinational chemical and consumer goods company, sees China as both a market and an innovation hub, Kohleick said. Its local research, manufacturing and technical-service capabilities allow solutions developed and validated in China to be deployed through regional networks, serving markets across the Asia-Pacific region with consistent quality and speed, he added. For APEC economies with abundant renewable energy resources, Chinese technology and capital can help convert those resources into local economic opportunities, from electric vehicle supply chains to renewable power projects and data centers. Fonterra, a New Zealand dairy cooperative owned by farmers, provides an example of how such industry links can support the low-carbon transition. Teh-han Chow, CEO of Fonterra China, said that a China-made electric boiler installed at Fonterra's Edendale site in New Zealand had replaced coal-fired equipment, reducing the emissions from milk processing. This project shows how cooperation across the Asia-Pacific region can draw on complementary strengths to accelerate the transition to a low-carbon economy while maintaining reliable and efficient production, he said.

item.title: Send-off ceremony held for Shenzhou XXIV astronauts
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
The three astronauts of the Shenzhou XXIV mission, including the first foreign national to be launched by a Chinese rocket, have headed to the launch tower at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China's Gobi Desert, after attending a send-off ceremony early on Wednesday morning. At the ceremony in front of their residential building starting at 5:28 am local time, mission commander Major General Tang Hongbo, spaceflight engineer Colonel Wu Yi, and Wing Commander Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a Pakistani astronaut and payload specialist in the mission, all in their spacesuits, reported to a high-ranking official that they were ready for the coming mission and asked for permission to embark on the flight. The official granted ceremonial departure clearance to the Shenzhou XXIV crew, who greeted and saluted all participants in the brief event, before boarding a coach to the launch tower. Many Jiuquan spaceport workers and residents stood along the road and hailed the astronauts as their vehicle passed. The upcoming mission marks the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space program. Ali will also become the first foreigner to visit China's Tiangong space station. The Long March 2F rocket tasked with transporting the astronauts to orbit stands at 58.3 meters and weighs nearly 500 metric tons. The model has carried out all of China's 17 manned flights so far.

item.title: From punk to rap, women upend cliches
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
"Yesterday, another one of my girlfriends died. The day before, we were still blaming her for not being there, saying we couldn't get a full table of mahjong without her. One by one, they've all gone … I'm terribly afraid of dying." The words are delivered in a strong regional accent over a rap beat by a woman in her 60s. There is no cool music video, choreographed performance or manufactured hip-hop image. Instead, she speaks openly about death, friendship and the people disappearing from her life. The song, Yesterday, Another One of My Girlfriends Died, is the work of Gui Xiang, a 62-year-old woman from Suzhou, Jiangsu province, who has found an unlikely fan base through rap. Her unconventional performances are growing in popularity on Chinese social media, where her age, raw delivery, accent and irreverent humor defy images usually associated with hip-hop artists. She has 215,000 followers on Xiaohongshu (Red-Note) and 575,000 on Douyin, where her videos have accumulated more than 12.35 million likes. Gui is part of a growing cohort of middle-aged and older Chinese women indulging in unexpected musical roles, from rappers and rock musicians to singers who have turned public parks into their stages. Their stories point to a broader shift in how some Chinese women are approaching later stages of life. Instead of restricting their leisure activities to familiar pursuits, such as square dancing in public parks, practicing tai chi or doing morning exercises and looking after grandchildren, they are experimenting with fresh artistic expression, including genres and subcultures traditionally associated with younger people. A growing interest in tech skills and an appetite for late-life learning are also improving their capabilities to pursue new interests. The 2025 New Silver Generation Lifestyle Report, published by Beijing News, found that more than half of the respondents — those aged over 60 — had attended or were attending interest classes or training courses. Nearly one-fifth were learning new skills, ranging from using digital devices and photography to handicrafts and short-video editing. The report also found that short-video platforms have become an important part of older people's lives, with nearly 60 percent of respondents using platforms such as Douyin and Kuaishou. Sociologist Zhang Hexuan, who holds a doctorate from University College London, said this generation is entering old age equipped with new digital tools and skills. They have diverse sources of information and a strong desire to explore, he said, while retaining a preference for social interaction and collective activities. "Personal growth and a sense of belonging to a group are developing simultaneously in this generation," he said. China's community networks provide a foundation for the more varied, multi-interest lifestyles they are seeking, Zhang added.

item.title: Pakistani astronaut to be first foreigner aboard Tiangong
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
China's Tiangong space station is poised to welcome its first foreign visitor — Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali — who will also become the first Pakistani citizen to reach Earth's orbit. The wing commander in the Pakistan Air Force is set to fly to the massive orbital outpost with two Chinese astronauts — Major General Tang Hongbo, commander of the Shenzhou XXIV mission, and Colonel Wu Yi, the crew's spaceflight engineer. According to Zhang Jingbo, a senior engineer and spokesman for the China Manned Space Agency, their spacecraft is scheduled to lift off aboard a Long March 2F rocket at 8:18 am on Wednesday from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China. At a news conference on Tuesday morning at the Jiuquan spaceport, Zhang told reporters that after the Shenzhou XXIV spacecraft reaches its preset orbital position, it will activate its rapid autonomous rendezvous and docking mode, taking about three-and-a-half hours to approach and dock with the front port of the Tianhe core module. After several days of handover work, the Shenzhou XXIV crew will take over the space station from the crew members of the Shenzhou XXIII mission, who would have spent six months in orbit, Zhang said. Tang and his crewmates are tasked with maintaining the station's routine operations; carrying out repairs and regular inspections to ensure its safe, reliable and efficient operation; advancing scientific research and applications; and participating in science communication, educational and public welfare activities. Ali will undertake a short-duration spaceflight as a payload specialist, Zhang said. "While in orbit, in addition to taking part in the crew's routine work, he will primarily be responsible for China-Pakistan joint space science experiments, focusing on installing experiment samples and units and conducting in-orbit tests," he said. After the handover, Colonel Zhu Yangzhu, commander of the Shenzhou XXIII mission, will remain aboard the station to complete China's first yearlong orbital mission. The Pakistani astronaut will return to Earth with the other two Shenzhou XXIII crewmembers, Zhang said. Orbital partnership In February 2025, the China Manned Space Agency and Pakistan's Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission signed an agreement in the Pakistani capital of Islamabad, launching bilateral cooperation in the process of selecting and training Pakistani astronauts. Following a rigorous three-stage selection process — preliminary, secondary and final — Muhammad Zeeshan Ali and Khurram Daud, both Pakistani military pilots, emerged from a pool of roughly 20 finalists selected from an initial group of aviators and scientists. Candidates were assessed for medical fitness, psychological resilience and their ability to withstand g-forces, according to officials with the Pakistani commission. The two men arrived in Beijing in April for intensive training at the Astronaut Center of China. Zhang said the joint mission "marks another landmark achievement of bilateral cooperation as China and Pakistan celebrate the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic ties, and a powerful testament to the time-honored friendship between the two nations". On major international social media platforms, many users identifying themselves as Pakistani nationals expressed anticipation, excitement and joy, and offered their blessings. Many also thanked China for including a Pakistani astronaut in its spaceflight mission. For Tang, the mission will mark another professional milestone: He will become the first astronaut to have participated in three missions aboard the Tiangong space station. During his first spaceflight, the three-month Shenzhou XII mission launched in June 2021, the Hunan native became one of the first inhabitants of the Chinese space station. Two years later, he commanded the six-month-long Shenzhou XVII mission, becoming the first astronaut to return to Tiangong.

item.title: Launch of Shenzhou XXIV crewed spaceship a complete success
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
China's Shenzhou XXIV crew is on its way to the Tiangong space station. A Long March 2F rocket lifted off from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center at 8:18 am Beijing time on Nov 25, sending the spacecraft into orbit. On board are Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, who will become the first foreign astronaut to visit Tiangong.

item.title: Cook Islands scientist joins historic deep-sea dive
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
A scientist from the Cook Islands has become the first person from her country to directly observe the deep-sea seabed within its exclusive economic zone, joining a dive aboard China's manned submersible Jiaolong in the Manihiki fracture zone on Nov 21 local time, the Ministry of Natural Resources said on Tuesday. Chloe Wragg joined Chinese scientists Yang Yifan and Zhao Shengya aboard the submersible to conduct an environmental survey. The mission successfully achieved its objectives, collecting valuable deep-sea environmental data and samples. The successful dive highlights the blue partnership between China and the Cook Islands and further strengthens their cooperation in deep-sea science and technology, the ministry said. Following the dive, Wragg expressed her excitement at witnessing the milestone firsthand. She said the Cook Islands has long been at the forefront of deep-sea scientific research and that the dive demonstrated the country's determination and commitment to deepening its understanding of its own seabed. She also expressed her gratitude for the opportunity to work with colleagues from the National Deep Sea Center and the Second Institute of Oceanography, both under the Ministry of Natural Resources. Wragg said the expedition reflected the longstanding friendship and scientific ties between the two countries, as well as their close relations and extensive exchanges. The expedition marks the second joint marine scientific mission between China and the Cook Islands, following their first such mission in 2025. During the current expedition, Jiaolong is scheduled to conduct five dives in the Cook Islands' exclusive economic zone. The mission aims to help the country fill gaps in its basic deep-sea data and train its first group of local researchers in crewed submersible operations through hands-on experience.

item.title: Nvidia-linked stocks post major gains
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
Nvidia-linked Chinese tech stocks surged on Tuesday after the United States chip company reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. However, analysts cautioned that Huang's return does not signal any easing of US restrictions on advanced chip exports to China, and that Beijing must redouble its efforts to domestically develop artificial intelligence chips. Foxconn Industrial Internet Co, a key Nvidia supplier, reached the daily trading limit of 10 percent at the Shanghai Stock Exchange within five minutes of opening, before closing the day with gains of around 7 percent. Meanwhile, Shenzhen Aoni Electronic Co jumped 20 percent and Victory Giant Technology gained more than 6 percent at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange. The gains were triggered by Nvidia's announcement late on Monday that its board had unanimously voted to restore Huang's roles as president, CEO and board member, less than two weeks after his resignation. Nvidia shares closed up 31.48 percent on the day, adding roughly $952 billion in market value in a single session — the largest one-day gain for a US company on record. Roger Sheng, vice-president of the US research firm Gartner, said, "Huang's return is definitely good news for Chinese companies embedded in Nvidia's industrial chain, as well as for global AI investment, as it eliminates a major uncertainty. At the very least, it serves as a buffer against the US AI bubble bursting too quickly." Data from JPMorgan Asset Management showed that the estimated AI capital expenditure of major US hyperscale cloud providers in 2026 is $799 billion, compared with $75 billion in China. But analysts also warned that the underlying policy environment has not changed. During Huang's absence, Nvidia announced that it would stop selling its custom-made H200 AI chips to China, closing a special supply channel that Huang had personally negotiated with the US government. The company has also established a committee for security and export control oversight — a new standing committee responsible for overseeing the company's export control compliance at the board level. "None of that will change in the short term just because Huang is back. Instead, Huang will handle China-related business more cautiously, which only further underlines the need for China to strengthen domestic substitution," Sheng said. Meanwhile, amid persisting US curbs, China's domestic AI chip industry has made measurable progress. Nvidia's share of China's data center AI chip market fell to 34 percent in the first half of this year — a significant drop from its previous near-monopoly levels. Huawei's share rose to 28 percent, and the domestic sector as a whole now commands a clear majority, with nine of 11 domestic chipmakers posting year-on-year growth in shipments, according to data from US market research firm International Data Corp. Core advantages in AI A senior executive of a Chinese large language model company, speaking to China Daily on condition of anonymity, said that domestically produced AI chips have already been used in AI inference — a relatively simple task — on scale, and that some chips are also being used for training, which is more demanding. In other words, Chinese AI chips have, to some extent, gained greater recognition from large language model companies. "The saga of Huang's departure and return has underscored the turbulence in the global semiconductor supply chain. In a world of intertwined change and upheaval, China's AI industry and its chip sector can move forward hand in hand and carve out a path of their own," the executive said. Hua Ning, senior director of Asia-Pacific business operations at the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, the world's largest organization of technical professionals, said China has three core advantages in AI. "First, government policy guidance; second, China's massive and unparalleled scale of engineers; and third, China's very comprehensive industrial chain. Such strengths make the country a crucial player on the global AI stage," Hua said. Charlie Dai, vice-president and principal analyst at market research company Forrester, said, "Huang's return shows that he remains the central figure on Nvidia's technology road map, ecosystem building and customer confidence. However, the more realistic risks include customers developing their own chips, export controls, intensifying competition and fluctuations in the AI infrastructure investment cycle." masi@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: From cuisine to tech: China-France cooperation blossoms
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-24
David Taupiac, secretary of the French National Assembly and member of the National Assembly for Gers, said in an interview with China Daily that China-France cooperation is flourishing across a wide range of fields and holds tremendous potential, from shared favorites such as wine and duck to cutting-edge industries including the French aeronautical sector and China's electric vehicle and robotics industries.
